A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching methods and core experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original FashionMNIST, SVHN, and CIFAR-10 experiments, aggregation analyses in Appendix C, and an MNIST incremental-learning experiment in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds client-level fairness results and a Bayesian-layer sensitivity study in Section 5.5 and Appendix D.2.

M1.justification: The IVON learning procedure, covariance-based aggregation, and projection-as-barycenter personalization remain unchanged. The foundation-model discussion applies existing barycenter operations conceptually; the new hybrid Bayesian-layer study explicitly excludes the proposed IVON method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate FashionMNIST, SVHN, CIFAR-10, and the two-task MNIST incremental-learning scenario. The added fairness analyses use existing datasets. Foundation-model merging is discussed without new experiments, and the Gaussian barycenter illustration does not introduce a new benchmark task.

E2.justification: FedAvg, pFedBayes, FedPop, and pFedVEM retain their participation in the corresponding main comparisons; FedPop remains excluded from global-model comparisons. Appendix D.2 compares hybrid BA-BFL with FedAvg but explicitly excludes the proposed IVON method, so it does not expand that method's evaluated baseline set.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a fairness evaluation using mean and worst-10% client accuracy, plus a controlled sweep over zero to three Bayesian layers in hybrid BA-BFL. This adds a distinct evaluation design that excludes IVON to avoid optimizer confounding. The original ten-client Dirichlet partitioning with beta=0.5 and IVON hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.5 and Appendix D add analyses of worst-client performance and whether increasing Bayesian-layer count improves fairness. Appendix C additionally displays FashionMNIST and SVHN personalization-parameter sweeps, which v1 discussed but did not plot. The original aggregation analysis and MNIST case study are retained.

E5.justification: v2 corrects the Wilcoxon figure caption from 'rank-sum' to 'signed-rank,' matching the test already described in v1's prose. This clarifies statistical reporting without establishing a changed test procedure. The main comparison still reports means and standard deviations over three independent runs.

E6.justification: All 162 mean/standard-deviation pairs in v1 Table 1 and v2 Table 2 match. However, v2 adds worst-client results, Bayesian-layer sensitivity outcomes, and explicit FashionMNIST/SVHN personalization curves in Figures 4 and 7–9. A new finding is that increasing Bayesian-layer count produces no consistent fairness trend.

T1.justification: Appendix A replaces the brief Lagrangian argument with a substantive KKT derivation and discussion of Slater conditions and strong duality. Remark 1 corrects the radius bound from D(pk||pg) to D(pg||pk). Appendices E.1 and F add mathematical characterizations of mixture/product barycenters and the Gaussian approximation to the forward-KL barycenter.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims of training-free personalization, projection–barycenter equivalence, and a favorable local/global performance trade-off. Added fairness evidence and application discussions do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds fairness interpretations, possible task dependence of Bayesian-layer effects, and an explicit rationale for concentrating on cross-silo evaluation. Appendix E.1 discusses architectural alignment requirements and untested large-scale applicability of model merging. Appendix F explains why the Gaussian forward-KL approximation can violate parameter independence.

D1.justification: v2 newly supplies a code-repository link and explicitly states that personalization occurs after FL training. It also clarifies the diagonal Hessian representation. The IVON hyperparameter table is unchanged and moves from v1 Appendix B into the main experimental section.

R1.justification: New discussions substantially broaden positioning around fairness, foundation-model merging, and Bayesian/multimodal barycenters. Added references include Chzhen et al., Gaucher et al., Matena and Raffel, Wortsman et al., Backhoff-Veraguas et al., and Qiu et al. Ekeland and Temam additionally supports the revised proof.

P1.justification: Extensive prose revisions throughout the introduction, background, method, and experiments accompany substantial restructuring. Hyperparameters move into the main text, a fairness subsection is added, and v1's broader-applicability appendix is redistributed between v2 Section 6 and Appendix E, alongside several new appendix sections.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column format to a single-column journal layout, reflowing and resizing existing displays. v2 adds Figures 4, 7–9, and 11, relocates the hyperparameter table, and renumbers the retained aggregation and incremental-learning figures without replacing their results.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful fairness and sensitivity evidence, displays previously unshown personalization curves, and improves transparency through code-access information and explicit applicability limits. These are incremental gains: the principal benchmark evidence is unchanged, foundation-model merging remains untested, and the expanded Appendix A proof still leaves Slater's condition unjustified at the allowed zero-radius boundary.
